event.label: Nuclear warnings and possible responses
event.description: How selected articles describe Russian nuclear threats, US warnings, possible responses and escalation risks. These are statements and forecasts, not reports that a nuclear weapon has been used.

topics.label: US warnings and response plans
topics.scope_note: The same Blinken interview may be repeated by several outlets. An undisclosed plan and an anonymous report about possible responses can coexist.

topics.label: How serious is the danger?
topics.scope_note: Future risk is different from observed preparations; no public report is not proof that no preparations exist.

topics.label: Russia’s stated nuclear policy
topics.scope_note: An unchanged doctrine does not itself deny threatening rhetoric or rule out use under that doctrine.

topics.label: Support for Ukraine under nuclear pressure
topics.scope_note: Compare stated policy recommendations, not a permanent outlet stance.

topics.label: Who is blamed for escalation?
topics.scope_note: Several causes may coexist. Blaming Washington or Putin is not automatically a logical contradiction.

method.country_note: Outlet countries describe origin. Claimant countries describe an office, organization or stated residence, not assumed citizenship.
method.claim_type_note: A fact claim is a checkable statement, not a fact verified by this graph. Opinions, predictions, legal positions and promises are marked separately.
method.edge_note: Green arrows point from a supporting claim to the claim receiving support. Grey comparisons have no assigned direction. Solid red arrows point from a source claim to a target claim it is proposed to contradict. Red direction follows the analyst-assigned comparison order. Every proposed conflict retains its reasoning and scope limits for human review.
method.attention_note: Attention is a qualitative reading of the saved article, with paragraph locators; it is not a measured share of words.
method.endorsement_note: A quoted speaker’s view is separate from the article narrator’s view. No outlet-wide position is inferred from one article.
method.cleaning_note: Uses saved recovered text. Kyiv Independent later Most Popular / News Feed material is excluded; original paragraph numbers retained. FT wrapped lines are joined into logical paragraphs. CNN is one long recovered paragraph: exact sentence excerpts are supplied. Sputnik’s missing headline-related Kremlin response is not invented.
